problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $S(3,-1,0)$ and is parallel to the vectors ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$  and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$

activity_context.topic_title: The Parametric Equations of a Plane

feedback.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(2,-3,4)$ and is parallel to the vectors ${v}_{1}=⟨1,5,-1⟩$  and ${v}_{2}=⟨1,2.5,1⟩.$
feedback.worked_solution:
A parametric equation of a plane is given by 

$$
r=p+sb+tc,
$$

where $p$ is the position vector of a point on the plane and the vectors $b$ and $c$ are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

Here, the position vector of the given point $P$ is $p=⟨2,-3,4⟩$ and the two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other) are ${v}_{1}=⟨1,5,-1⟩$  and ${v}_{2}=⟨1,2.5,1⟩.$

So, a parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
r=⟨2,-3,4⟩+s⟨1,5,-1⟩+t⟨1,2.5,1⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
